body.why_ranked_1_not_appended_at_the_bottom: This is the only vector in the full set (RT00-RT08) that is LIVE and actively compounding at write time rather than a forensic reconstruction of a past session -- every hourly Nidhoggr fire adds one more stalled window, unbounded, for as long as the operator is away. It also sharpens RT01 rather than duplicating it: RT01 shows a scheduler that mostly does NOT fire (78/81 Claude-Desktop schtasks disabled); RT00 shows a DIFFERENT substrate whose scheduler DOES fire on cadence and still fails one layer downstream, at the authorization gate -- meaning the RT01 cure (build working cadence) is necessary but demonstrably not sufficient.

No live check was run against Codex desktop, Claude Desktop scheduled tasks, or the $0-mesh LiteLLM proxy for the same per-fire-authorization failure class -- these are flagged, not confirmed, per the operator's own framing of the attack class as extending beyond Antigravity.

next_safe_action: If a screenshot file or Antigravity session/conversation log becomes readable by an agent, re-verify RT00 directly and upgrade claim_status to wired_with_receipts (or correct it) rather than leaving it on operator testimony alone. honest_flaw: I am ranking a vector I did not personally observe above five vectors I verified first-hand from repo artifacts, on operator authority and internal consistency alone. That is the correct call under this fleet's L31 doctrine (operator's technical claims are operative spec, not expertise to merely respect) and under 'take what is given, verify always' -- but it is worth naming plainly that RT00's evidentiary standing is categorically different from RT01-RT08, and the report says so in two places now (addendum + honest-flaw section) specifically so a reader cannot mistake rank-1 placement for strongest-verification placement.
